Just a minute before the break, Davy Klaassen restored parity in the 44th minute, converting a chance set up by Youri Regeer to ensure the sides went into halftime level. The Oscar Gloukh Show The second half saw the momentum shift drastically as Oscar Gloukh took center stage. In the 53rd minute, Gloukh clinical finishing put Ajax ahead for the first time, assisted by Mika Godts . He didn't stop there, doubling his tally in the 58th minute after being played through by Steven Berghuis . The Serbian side attempted to regain composure with multiple substitutions, but the Dutch giants were in full flow, dictating the tempo across every sector of the pitch. Completing the Hat-trick The night was truly defined by Gloukh’s clinical nature. In the 71st minute, he completed a spectacular hat-trick, this time aided by an assist from substitute Oliver Edvardsen . Following his third goal, Gloukh was given a well-deserved rest, replaced by Abdellah Ouazane . Despite late yellow cards for Vojvodina's Stefan Mitrovic and Milan Kolarevic , Ajax remained composed to see out the match and secure a convincing victory on the European stage.
